# B"H
<!-- Boruch Hashem -->
<!-- Blessed is He -->

# Icon Policy Delta

> The Awtsmoos reveals a sign without weakening the gate that guards all media;
> Awtsmoos.com lets one self-contained data icon answer Chrome without policy amnesia.

## New Evidence

- Root `.gitignore` lines 124–148 intentionally deny all common image, media, document, and model formats unless an explicit source root opens them.
- `*.svg`, `*.png`, and `*.ico` are all denied globally.
- Moving the icon to another folder does not change that policy.
- Force-adding the icon would bypass rather than reveal an approved source-root exception.
- Editing the large global ignore file would widen scope and violate the small route-hardening boundary.

## Improved Final Decision

1. Delete the ignored draft SVG file.
2. Rewrite `index.html` with one explicit self-contained `data:image/svg+xml` favicon.
3. Keep the data icon script-free, font-free, image-free, and network-free.
4. Rewrite the route-shell test to decode and inspect the embedded SVG.
5. Preserve the refreshed handoff files unchanged.
6. Verify the browser makes no `/favicon.ico` request after deployment.

## Final Source Scope

- `index.html`
- `experiments/Awtsmoos/src/test/launcher/mitzvahWorldRouteShell.test.mjs`
- `NEXT_AI_README.md`
- `REMAINING_WORK.md`

No binary or ignored media file enters Git.
